adds.title: Transgender legal history in the United States (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia's survey of US transgender legal history documents the shifting federal framework for housing trans prisoners: a January 2015 ICE memo directed housing transgender immigration detainees according to gender identity, and in 2016 the US Department of Justice released guidelines forbidding corrections agencies from assigning trans inmates to men's or women's units solely on birth anatomy. In 2018 the Federal Bureau of Prisons revised its Transgender Offender Manual the other direction - deleting the sentence that the Transgender Executive Council 'will recommend housing by gender identity when appropriate' and instead making placement 'a case-by-case basis' in which 'biological sex' is 'the initial determination', with gender identity used only 'in rare cases'. No Delaware- or Maryland-specific placement policy is covered. Article last revised 2026-06-12; accessed 2026-10-04.

records.note: No Delaware-specific data on trans prisoner placement was found within the allowed budget (one Wikipedia full-text search, two candidate fetches). The second candidate fetch - a supposed Wikipedia article on the best-known suspected Delaware trans-prisoner case - returned a Wikipedia redlink (no such article exists), so no case-level source could be verified and nothing from it was added (cache 14d25bebca453d30, marked error=redlink). The one verified source documents the national framework applying to US custody: 2015 ICE identity-based housing memo, 2016 DOJ guidance against placement solely on birth anatomy, and the 2018 Federal Bureau of Prisons Transgender Offender Manual revision making birth sex the initial determination with gender identity only in rare cases. Whether and how Delaware's Department of Correction applies that framework, and whether any Delaware case or segregation practice exists, remains unresearched in this lane.

adds.title: Transgender rights in the United States (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia's US transgender-rights article documents the nationally reported experience of trans women held in men's facilities, including the V-coding practice of assigning trans women to aggressive cisgender male cellmates ('a central part of a trans woman's sentence'), and reports that trans women who physically resist sexual assault are often criminally charged with assault and placed in solitary confinement, with the charge then used to extend the sentence and deny parole. A 2021 California study cited in the article found 69% of surveyed trans women prisoners reported being made to perform unwanted sexual acts, 58.5% reported violent sexual assault, and 88% reported a 'marriage-like relationship'. The article records no Maryland-specific placement rule, special unit, or named case. Article last revised 2026-10-04; accessed 2026-10-04.

records.note: Both permitted Wikipedia candidates for Maryland were fetched/verified (the legal-history article and the Transgender-rights article, the latter reused from the site fetch cache), but they document only national-level material: the 2015-2018 federal placement-policy arc (identity-based guidance; 2016 DOJ no-birth-anatomy rule; 2018 BOP manual revision to 'biological sex as the initial determination') and the nationally documented segregation practice of charging trans women who resist assault with assault and isolating them in solitary confinement. No Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services placement policy, special unit, solitary/segregation rule, or documented trans-prisoner case/ruling was found within the allowed one-search/two-fetch budget, and the batch's Maryland record likewise carries no prison-housing data - the gap stands unfilled pending a wider lane.
